# `Q-22-7` — Double Subscript Or Superscript

> A base has two superscripts (`x^2^3`) or two subscripts (`x_1_2`) in a row.

## What this means

A base takes at most one `^` and one `_`. TeX rejects a second one outright; quarto-math keeps the first script, reports the second, and falls back to verbatim source in formats that need a conversion.

## Why this happens

Common causes: a missing brace group (`x^2^3` when `x^{2^3}` or `{x^2}^3` was meant), or a macro that expands to a script applied to something that already has one.

## How to fix it

Group the intended structure with braces: `x^{2^3}` for a tower, `{x^2}^3` for a script on a scripted base.

## Where it is reported

Math diagnostics point into the `.qmd` at the exact characters inside the
`$…$` or `$$…$$` block, including math that spans several lines or sits
inside a block quote or list item. When a `\newcommand` macro is involved,
a problem inside the macro body points at the definition and a problem in
a macro argument points at the use.
